141: ਹਕੁ ਪਰਾਇਆ. ਨਾਨਕਾ; ਉਸੁ ਸੂਅਰ. ਉਸੁ ਗਾਇ ॥
O Nanak, to take what rightly belongs to another is like pork to the Muslim and beef to the Hindu.
ਗੁਰੁ ਪੀਰੁ ਹਾਮਾ ਤਾ ਭਰੇ; ਜਾ. ਮੁਰਦਾਰੁ ਨ ਖਾਇ ॥
The Guru, the spiritual guide, stands by you only if you do not eat what is not yours.
ਗਲੀ. ਭਿਸਤਿ ਨ ਜਾਈਐ; ਛੁਟੈ. ਸਚੁ ਕਮਾਇ ॥
By mere talk one does not reach paradise; one is saved only by practising truth.
ਮਾਰਣ ਪਾਹਿ ਹਰਾਮ ਮਹਿ; ਹੋਇ ਹਲਾਲੁ ਨ ਜਾਇ ॥
Adding spices to forbidden food does not make it lawful.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਗਲੀ ਕੂੜੀਈ; ਕੂੜੋ ਪਲੈ ਪਾਇ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, from false talk only falsehood is obtained. ॥2॥
ਪੰਜਿ ਨਿਵਾਜਾ. ਵਖਤ ਪੰਜਿ; ਪੰਜਾ ਪੰਜੇ ਨਾਉ ॥
There are five prayers, five times of prayer, and the five have five names.
ਪਹਿਲਾ ਸਚੁ ਹਲਾਲ ਦੁਇ; ਤੀਜਾ ਖੈਰ ਖੁਦਾਇ ॥
Let the first be truth, the second honest earning, the third charity in God's name,
ਚਉਥੀ ਨੀਅਤਿ ਰਾਸਿ ਮਨੁ; ਪੰਜਵੀ ਸਿਫਤਿ ਸਨਾਇ ॥
the fourth a pure intention and mind, and the fifth the praise and glory of God.
ਕਰਣੀ ਕਲਮਾ ਆਖਿ ਕੈ; ਤਾ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਣੁ ਸਦਾਇ ॥
Let good deeds be your creed; then you may call yourself a Muslim.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਜੇਤੇ ਕੂੜਿਆਰ; ਕੂੜੈ ਕੂੜੀ ਪਾਇ ॥੩॥
O Nanak, all the false gain only falsehood, and only false honour. ॥3॥
ਇਕਿ ਰਤਨ ਪਦਾਰਥ ਵਣਜਦੇ; ਇਕਿ ਕਚੈ ਦੇ ਵਾਪਾਰਾ ॥
Some trade in priceless jewels, and some deal in glass.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰਿ ਤੁਠੈ ਪਾਈਅਨਿ; ਅੰਦਰਿ ਰਤਨ ਭੰਡਾਰਾ ॥
When the True Guru is pleased, the treasure of jewels within is found.
ਵਿਣੁ ਗੁਰ. ਕਿਨੈ ਨ ਲਧਿਆ; ਅੰਧੇ. ਭਉਕਿ ਮੁਏ ਕੂੜਿਆਰਾ ॥
Without the Guru no one has found it; the blind, false ones have died barking (begging from door to door).
ਮਨਮੁਖ ਦੂਜੈ ਪਚਿ ਮੁਏ; ਨਾ ਬੂਝਹਿ ਵੀਚਾਰਾ ॥
The self-willed are consumed by duality; they do not understand reflection.
ਇਕਸੁ ਬਾਝਹੁ. ਦੂਜਾ ਕੋ ਨਹੀ; ਕਿਸੁ ਅਗੈ ਕਰਹਿ ਪੁਕਾਰਾ ॥
Without the One there is no other; before whom can they cry out?
ਇਕਿ ਨਿਰਧਨ. ਸਦਾ ਭਉਕਦੇ; ਇਕਨਾ ਭਰੇ ਤੁਜਾਰਾ ॥
Some are destitute and forever wander begging; others have treasuries overflowing.
ਵਿਣੁ ਨਾਵੈ. ਹੋਰੁ ਧਨੁ ਨਾਹੀ; ਹੋਰੁ ਬਿਖਿਆ ਸਭੁ ਛਾਰਾ ॥
Without the Name there is no other wealth; all else is poison and ashes.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਆਪਿ ਕਰਾਏ ਕਰੇ ਆਪਿ; ਹੁਕਮਿ ਸਵਾਰਣਹਾਰਾ ॥੭॥
O Nanak, He Himself acts and causes others to act; by His command He adorns us. ॥7॥
ਮੁਸਲਮਾਣੁ. ਕਹਾਵਣੁ ਮੁਸਕਲੁ; ਜਾ ਹੋਇ ਤਾ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਣੁ ਕਹਾਵੈ ॥
It is difficult to be called a Muslim; only one who truly is one may be called a Muslim.
ਅਵਲਿ ਅਉਲਿ ਦੀਨੁ ਕਰਿ ਮਿਠਾ; ਮਸਕਲ ਮਾਨਾ. ਮਾਲੁ ਮੁਸਾਵੈ ॥
First let him find the faith sweet, and let his wealth be scraped clean (shared), as rust is scraped off.
ਹੋਇ ਮੁਸਲਿਮੁ. ਦੀਨ ਮੁਹਾਣੈ; ਮਰਣ ਜੀਵਣ ਕਾ ਭਰਮੁ ਚੁਕਾਵੈ ॥
Becoming a true follower of the faith, let him set aside delusion about life and death.
ਰਬ ਕੀ ਰਜਾਇ. ਮੰਨੇ ਸਿਰ ਉਪਰਿ; ਕਰਤਾ ਮੰਨੇ. ਆਪੁ ਗਵਾਵੈ ॥
Let him accept God's will as supreme, believe in the Creator, and shed his self-conceit.
ਤਉ ਨਾਨਕ. ਸਰਬ ਜੀਆ ਮਿਹਰੰਮਤਿ ਹੋਇ; ਤ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਣੁ ਕਹਾਵੈ ॥੧॥
And when, O Nanak, he is merciful to all beings, then he may be called a Muslim. ॥1॥
ਪਰਹਰਿ ਕਾਮ ਕ੍ਰੋਧੁ ਝੂਠੁ ਨਿੰਦਾ; ਤਜਿ ਮਾਇਆ ਅਹੰਕਾਰੁ ਚੁਕਾਵੈ ॥
Forsaking lust, anger, falsehood and slander, abandoning Maya, one gets rid of ego.
ਤਜਿ ਕਾਮੁ ਕਾਮਿਨੀ. ਮੋਹੁ ਤਜੈ; ਤਾ ਅੰਜਨ ਮਾਹਿ. ਨਿਰੰਜਨੁ ਪਾਵੈ ॥
Abandoning sexual desire and attachment to woman, one finds the Pure Lord amid the darkness of Maya.
ਤਜਿ ਮਾਨੁ ਅਭਿਮਾਨੁ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਸੁਤ ਦਾਰਾ; ਤਜਿ ਪਿਆਸ ਆਸ. ਰਾਮ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਵੈ ॥
Abandoning pride, self-importance and attachment to children and spouse, abandoning thirst and hope, one is attuned to the Lord.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਸਾਚਾ ਮਨਿ ਵਸੈ; ਸਾਚ ਸਬਦਿ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮਿ ਸਮਾਵੈ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, the True One comes to dwell in the mind, and through the True Word one merges in the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
ਰਾਜੇ ਰਯਤਿ ਸਿਕਦਾਰ; ਕੋਇ. ਨ ਰਹਸੀਓ ॥
Neither kings, nor subjects, nor chiefs shall remain.
Shops, cities and bazaars shall crumble by His command.
ਪਕੇ ਬੰਕ ਦੁਆਰ; ਮੂਰਖੁ ਜਾਣੈ ਆਪਣੇ ॥
The fool thinks the solid, beautiful gates of his house are his own.
ਦਰਬਿ ਭਰੇ ਭੰਡਾਰ; ਰੀਤੇ ਇਕਿ ਖਣੇ ॥
Treasuries overflowing with wealth are emptied in an instant.
Fine horses, chariots, camels, elephants with their trappings,
ਬਾਗ ਮਿਲਖ ਘਰ ਬਾਰ; ਕਿਥੈ. ਸਿ ਆਪਣੇ ॥
gardens, lands, houses and homes — where are those things he called his own?
Tents, beds of fine tape, and satin pavilions — all shall pass.
O Nanak, the Giver alone is true; He is recognised through His creation. ॥8॥
ਨਦੀਆ ਹੋਵਹਿ ਧੇਣਵਾ; ਸੁੰਮ ਹੋਵਹਿ ਦੁਧੁ ਘੀਉ ॥
If the rivers became cows giving milk, and the springs became milk and ghee,
ਸਗਲੀ ਧਰਤੀ ਸਕਰ ਹੋਵੈ; ਖੁਸੀ ਕਰੇ ਨਿਤ ਜੀਉ ॥
if the whole earth became sugar, so that my soul might rejoice forever,
142: ਪਰਬਤੁ ਸੁਇਨਾ ਰੁਪਾ ਹੋਵੈ; ਹੀਰੇ ਲਾਲ ਜੜਾਉ ॥
if the mountains became gold and silver, studded with diamonds and rubies —
ਭੀ ਤੂੰਹੈ ਸਾਲਾਹਣਾ; ਆਖਣ. ਲਹੈ ਨ ਚਾਉ ॥੧॥
even then I would praise You, and my longing to chant Your praise would not end. ॥1॥
ਭਾਰ ਅਠਾਰਹ. ਮੇਵਾ ਹੋਵੈ; ਗਰੁੜਾ ਹੋਇ ਸੁਆਉ ॥
If all the vegetation became fruit, with the finest taste,
ਚੰਦੁ ਸੂਰਜੁ ਦੁਇ ਫਿਰਦੇ ਰਖੀਅਹਿ; ਨਿਹਚਲੁ ਹੋਵੈ ਥਾਉ ॥
if the sun and moon were kept circling in my service, and my abode were made permanent —
ਭੀ ਤੂੰਹੈ ਸਾਲਾਹਣਾ; ਆਖਣ. ਲਹੈ ਨ ਚਾਉ ॥੨॥
even then I would praise You, and my longing to chant Your praise would not end. ॥2॥
ਜੇ. ਦੇਹੈ ਦੁਖੁ ਲਾਈਐ; ਪਾਪ ਗਰਹ ਦੁਇ ਰਾਹੁ ॥
If my body were afflicted with pain, and the two evil stars, Rahu and Ketu, were upon me,
ਰਤੁ ਪੀਣੇ ਰਾਜੇ. ਸਿਰੈ ਉਪਰਿ ਰਖੀਅਹਿ; ਏਵੈ ਜਾਪੈ ਭਾਉ ॥
if bloodthirsty kings ruled over my head — if this were how Your love showed itself —
ਭੀ ਤੂੰਹੈ ਸਾਲਾਹਣਾ; ਆਖਣ. ਲਹੈ ਨ ਚਾਉ ॥੩॥
even then I would praise You, and my longing to chant Your praise would not end. ॥3॥
ਅਗੀ ਪਾਲਾ ਕਪੜੁ ਹੋਵੈ; ਖਾਣਾ ਹੋਵੈ ਵਾਉ ॥
If fire and frost were my clothing, and wind my food,
ਸੁਰਗੈ ਦੀਆ ਮੋਹਣੀਆ ਇਸਤਰੀਆ ਹੋਵਨਿ; ਨਾਨਕ. ਸਭੋ ਜਾਉ ॥
if the enticing nymphs of heaven were my wives — O Nanak, all this shall pass away —
ਭੀ ਤੂਹੈ ਸਾਲਾਹਣਾ; ਆਖਣ. ਲਹੈ ਨ ਚਾਉ ॥੪॥
even then I would praise You, and my longing to chant Your praise would not end. ॥4॥
One who commits evil deeds in secret, and does not know the Master as ever present,
ਸੋ ਕਹੀਐ ਦੇਵਾਨਾ; ਆਪੁ ਨ ਪਛਾਣਈ ॥
is called a madman; he does not recognise his own self.
Strife in the world is evil; one is consumed in quarrels.
Without the Name, in vice and doubt, one rots away.
ਰਾਹ ਦੋਵੈ. ਇਕੁ ਜਾਣੈ; ਸੋਈ ਸਿਝਸੀ ॥
Of the two paths, one who knows the One alone shall succeed.
The speaker of falsehood, engrossed in falsehood, shall burn.
For one absorbed in the True One, the whole world is beautiful.
Shedding self-conceit, one is acquitted at His door and in His court. ॥9॥
ਸੋ ਜੀਵਿਆ; ਜਿਸੁ ਮਨਿ ਵਸਿਆ ਸੋਇ ॥
He alone truly lives in whose mind the Lord dwells.
O Nanak, no one else truly lives.
If such a one lives, he departs in dishonour;
all that he eats is ill-gotten.
One who delights in power and delights in wealth,
intoxicated with these delights, dances shamelessly.
O Nanak, he is cheated and plundered;
without the Name he departs having lost his honour. ॥1॥
What use is food, what use are clothes,
if the True Lord does not dwell in the mind?
ਕਿਆ ਮੇਵਾ. ਕਿਆ ਘਿਉ ਗੁੜੁ ਮਿਠਾ; ਕਿਆ ਮੈਦਾ ਕਿਆ ਮਾਸੁ ॥
What use are fruits, ghee, sweet jaggery, fine flour or meat?
ਕਿਆ ਕਪੜੁ. ਕਿਆ ਸੇਜ ਸੁਖਾਲੀ; ਕੀਜਹਿ ਭੋਗ ਬਿਲਾਸ ॥
What use are fine clothes, a soft bed, and indulging in pleasures?
ਕਿਆ ਲਸਕਰ. ਕਿਆ ਨੇਬ ਖਵਾਸੀ; ਆਵੈ ਮਹਲੀ ਵਾਸੁ ॥
What use are armies, mace-bearers and servants, and living in mansions?
ਨਾਨਕ ਸਚੇ ਨਾਮ ਵਿਣੁ; ਸਭੇ ਟੋਲ ਵਿਣਾਸੁ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, without the True Name, all this paraphernalia shall perish. ॥2॥
ਜਾਤੀ ਦੈ ਕਿਆ ਹਥਿ; ਸਚੁ ਪਰਖੀਐ ॥
What can caste do? Truth is what is tested.
If one holds poison and tastes it, one dies (whatever one's caste).
ਸਚੇ ਕੀ ਸਿਰਕਾਰ; ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥
The rule of the True One is known throughout every age.
One who obeys His command is honoured at His door and in His court.
The Master has sent us into the world with the task of obeying His command.
The drummer, the Guru, has proclaimed this reflection through the Word.
Hearing it, some have mounted their horses, and some are getting ready;
some have loaded their baggage, and some have set off in haste. ॥10॥
ਜਾ ਪਕਾ. ਤਾ ਕਟਿਆ; ਰਹੀ. ਸੁ ਪਲਰਿ ਵਾੜਿ ॥
When the crop is ripe it is cut; only the stalks and the hedge remain standing.
ਸਣੁ ਕੀਸਾਰਾ. ਚਿਥਿਆ; ਕਣੁ ਲਇਆ. ਤਨੁ ਝਾੜਿ ॥
The ears are threshed, and the grain is separated from the chaff by winnowing.
ਦੁਇ ਪੁੜ ਚਕੀ ਜੋੜਿ ਕੈ; ਪੀਸਣ ਆਇ ਬਹਿਠੁ ॥
Placing the two millstones together, one sits down to grind the grain.
ਜੋ ਦਰਿ ਰਹੇ. ਸੁ ਉਬਰੇ; ਨਾਨਕ. ਅਜਬੁ ਡਿਠੁ ॥੧॥
Those grains that stay at the centre (by the pivot) are spared — O Nanak, I have seen this wonder! ॥1॥
ਵੇਖੁ ਜਿ ਮਿਠਾ ਕਟਿਆ; ਕਟਿ ਕੁਟਿ ਬਧਾ ਪਾਇ ॥
See how the sugarcane is cut; stripped and trimmed, it is bound into bundles.
143: ਖੁੰਢਾ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਰਖਿ ਕੈ; ਦੇਨਿ. ਸੁ ਮਲ ਸਜਾਇ ॥
Placing it between the rollers, the strong men punish it (by crushing it).
ਰਸੁ ਕਸੁ ਟਟਰਿ ਪਾਈਐ; ਤਪੈ ਤੈ ਵਿਲਲਾਇ ॥
All the juice is put in the cauldron; heated, it boils and wails.
ਭੀ ਸੋ ਫੋਗੁ ਸਮਾਲੀਐ; ਦਿਚੈ ਅਗਿ ਜਾਲਾਇ ॥
Even the crushed husk is gathered up, dried, and burnt in the fire beneath.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਮਿਠੈ ਪਤਰੀਐ; ਵੇਖਹੁ ਲੋਕਾ ਆਇ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, come and see, O people: this is how one is ruined for the sake of sweetness. ॥2॥
ਇਕਨਾ. ਮਰਣੁ ਨ ਚਿਤਿ; ਆਸ ਘਣੇਰਿਆ ॥
Some do not think of death; they cherish great hopes.
ਮਰਿ ਮਰਿ ਜੰਮਹਿ ਨਿਤ; ਕਿਸੈ ਨ ਕੇਰਿਆ ॥
They die and are born again and again, every day; they are of use to no one.
In their own mind and heart they call themselves good.
But the King of Death keeps his eye on those self-willed ones all the time.
ਮਨਮੁਖ ਲੂਣ ਹਾਰਾਮ; ਕਿਆ ਨ ਜਾਣਿਆ ॥
The self-willed are faithless to the salt they eat; they do not appreciate what the Lord has done for them.
ਬਧੇ ਕਰਨਿ ਸਲਾਮ; ਖਸਮ. ਨ ਭਾਣਿਆ ॥
They bow only under compulsion, and so they cannot please the Master.
ਸਚੁ ਮਿਲੈ ਮੁਖਿ ਨਾਮੁ; ਸਾਹਿਬ ਭਾਵਸੀ ॥
One who meets the True One, with the Name on his lips, is pleasing to the Master.
People salute him on his throne; he receives what is written in his destiny. ॥11॥
ਮਛੀ ਤਾਰੂ. ਕਿਆ ਕਰੇ; ਪੰਖੀ ਕਿਆ ਆਕਾਸੁ ॥
What can deep water do to a fish? What can the sky do to a bird?
ਪਥਰ ਪਾਲਾ ਕਿਆ ਕਰੇ; ਖੁਸਰੇ ਕਿਆ ਘਰ ਵਾਸੁ ॥
What can cold do to a stone? What does married life mean to a eunuch?
ਕੁਤੇ ਚੰਦਨੁ ਲਾਈਐ; ਭੀ ਸੋ ਕੁਤੀ ਧਾਤੁ ॥
You may anoint a dog with sandalwood, but its nature remains that of a dog.
ਬੋਲਾ. ਜੇ ਸਮਝਾਈਐ; ਪੜੀਅਹਿ ਸਿੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਿ ਪਾਠ ॥
You may instruct a deaf man and recite the Smritis before him (he cannot hear).
ਅੰਧਾ. ਚਾਨਣਿ ਰਖੀਐ; ਦੀਵੇ ਬਲਹਿ ਪਚਾਸ ॥
You may set a blind man in the light, with fifty lamps burning (he will see nothing).
ਚਉਣੇ ਸੁਇਨਾ ਪਾਈਐ; ਚੁਣਿ ਚੁਣਿ ਖਾਵੈ ਘਾਸੁ ॥
You may scatter gold before a grazing herd; it will still pick out and eat the grass.
ਲੋਹਾ ਮਾਰਣਿ ਪਾਈਐ; ਢਹੈ. ਨ ਹੋਇ ਕਪਾਸ ॥
You may reduce iron to a powder, yet it will not become soft like cotton.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਮੂਰਖ ਏਹਿ ਗੁਣ; ਬੋਲੇ ਸਦਾ ਵਿਣਾਸੁ ॥੧॥
O Nanak, such are the traits of a fool: whenever he speaks, it always does harm. ॥1॥
When bronze, gold or iron breaks,
the smith joins it again with fire.
When a husband is estranged from his wife,
in this world they are joined again through their children.
When the king makes a demand, the bond is restored when it is paid.
The starving man is joined (to his body) when he eats.
Famine is ended when the rains come and the rivers flow.
Love is bound together by sweet words.
One is joined to the Vedas (scriptures) when one speaks the truth.
The dead keep their bond with the world through goodness and charity.
Through such bonds the world carries on.
A fool's folly is checked only by a blow to the face.
through praise of the Lord, one is bound to His court. ॥2॥
ਆਪੇ ਕੁਦਰਤਿ ਸਾਜਿ ਕੈ; ਆਪੇ ਕਰੇ ਬੀਚਾਰੁ ॥
He Himself created the creation, and He Himself takes care of it.
ਇਕਿ ਖੋਟੇ ਇਕਿ ਖਰੇ; ਆਪੇ ਪਰਖਣਹਾਰੁ ॥
Some are counterfeit and some are genuine; He Himself is the Assayer.
ਖਰੇ. ਖਜਾਨੈ ਪਾਈਅਹਿ; ਖੋਟੇ. ਸਟੀਅਹਿ ਬਾਹਰ ਵਾਰਿ ॥
The genuine are placed in His treasury; the counterfeit are cast outside.
ਖੋਟੇ ਸਚੀ ਦਰਗਹ ਸੁਟੀਅਹਿ; ਕਿਸੁ ਆਗੈ ਕਰਹਿ ਪੁਕਾਰ ॥
The counterfeit are thrown out of the True Court; to whom can they complain?
ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਪਿਛੈ ਭਜਿ ਪਵਹਿ; ਏਹਾ ਕਰਣੀ ਸਾਰੁ ॥
Let them run and fall at the feet of the True Guru; this is the most excellent thing to do.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ. ਖੋਟਿਅਹੁ ਖਰੇ ਕਰੇ; ਸਬਦਿ ਸਵਾਰਣਹਾਰੁ ॥
The True Guru turns the counterfeit into genuine; through the Word he is able to reform them.
ਸਚੀ ਦਰਗਹ ਮੰਨੀਅਨਿ; ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਪਿਆਰਿ ॥
They are honoured in the True Court through the loving devotion the Guru gives.
ਗਣਤ ਤਿਨਾ ਦੀ ਕੋ ਕਿਆ ਕਰੇ; ਜੋ. ਆਪਿ ਬਖਸੇ ਕਰਤਾਰਿ ॥੧੨॥
Who can count the faults of those whom the Creator Himself has forgiven? ॥12॥
ਹਮ ਜੇਰ ਜਿਮੀ. ਦੁਨੀਆ; ਪੀਰਾ ਮਸਾਇਕਾ ਰਾਇਆ ॥
Pirs, shaikhs, rulers — the whole world ends up under the earth.
Even emperors pass away; You alone endure forever, O God —
Neither gods, nor demons, nor men,
nor Siddhas, nor seekers remain on the earth.
144: Neither the just who give judgment among men,
nor the seven underworlds beneath the earth shall remain.
Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the visible sky,
nor the seven continents, nor the waters,
nor food, nor wind — none of these is permanent.
The sustenance of beings is in no one else's hands.
All have hope in the One alone.
There is no other who is everlasting.
Birds have no money in their purses.
They rely only on the trees and water.
O Nanak, what is written on the forehead
He alone puts strength into beings, and He alone takes it away.
True is Your command; it is understood by facing the Guru.
Shedding self-conceit through the Guru's teaching, one recognises the True One.
True is Your court; the Word is the pass to reach it.
Reflecting on the True Word, one merges in the True One.
The self-willed are always false; they wander deluded by doubt.
ਵਿਸਟਾ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਵਾਸੁ; ਸਾਦੁ. ਨ ਜਾਣਿਆ ॥
They dwell in filth, and do not know the taste (of the Word).
ਵਿਣੁ ਨਾਵੈ ਦੁਖੁ ਪਾਇ; ਆਵਣ ਜਾਣਿਆ ॥
Without the Name they suffer, coming and going in birth and death.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਪਾਰਖੁ ਆਪਿ; ਜਿਨਿ. ਖੋਟਾ ਖਰਾ ਪਛਾਣਿਆ ॥੧੩॥
O Nanak, He Himself is the Assayer, who recognises the counterfeit and the genuine. ॥13॥
ਸੀਹਾ ਬਾਜਾ ਚਰਗਾ ਕੁਹੀਆ; ਏਨਾ ਖਵਾਲੇ ਘਾਹ ॥
If He wishes, He makes tigers, hawks, kestrels and falcons eat grass;
ਘਾਹੁ ਖਾਨਿ. ਤਿਨਾ ਮਾਸੁ ਖਵਾਲੇ; ਏਹਿ ਚਲਾਏ ਰਾਹ ॥
and those who eat grass, He makes them eat meat — such are the ways He sets.
ਨਦੀਆ ਵਿਚਿ. ਟਿਬੇ ਦੇਖਾਲੇ; ਥਲੀ ਕਰੇ ਅਸਗਾਹ ॥
He makes islands appear in flowing rivers, and turns deserts into deep waters.
ਕੀੜਾ ਥਾਪਿ ਦੇਇ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀ; ਲਸਕਰ ਕਰੇ ਸੁਆਹ ॥
He sets a worm upon the throne of kingship, and reduces armies to ashes.
ਜੇਤੇ ਜੀਅ. ਜੀਵਹਿ ਲੈ ਸਾਹਾ; ਜੀਵਾਲੇ. ਤਾ ਕਿ ਅਸਾਹ ॥
All beings live by drawing breath; but if He wishes to keep them alive, what need have they of breath?
ਨਾਨਕ. ਜਿਉ ਜਿਉ ਸਚੇ ਭਾਵੈ; ਤਿਉ ਤਿਉ ਦੇਇ ਗਿਰਾਹ ॥੧॥
O Nanak, as it pleases the True Lord, so He gives sustenance. ॥1॥
Some eat meat, and some eat grass.
Some receive all kinds of delicious foods,
while some live in the earth and eat earth.
Some practise breath control, absorbed in regulating the breath.
Some, worshippers of the Formless One, live by the support of the Name.
One who knows the Giver lives over his head does not die (spiritually).
ਨਾਨਕ. ਮੁਠੇ ਜਾਹਿ; ਨਾਹੀ. ਮਨਿ ਸੋਇ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, those are cheated in whose mind He does not dwell. ॥2॥
ਪੂਰੇ ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਕਾਰ; ਕਰਮਿ ਕਮਾਈਐ ॥
The work shown by the perfect Guru is done only by His grace.
Shedding self-conceit through the Guru's teaching, one meditates on the Name.
Engaged in other work, one wastes this human life.
ਵਿਣੁ ਨਾਵੈ. ਸਭ ਵਿਸੁ; ਪੈਝੈ ਖਾਈਐ ॥
Without the Name, all that one wears and eats is poison.
Praising the True Word, one merges in the True One.
ਵਿਣੁ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਸੇਵੇ. ਨਾਹੀ ਸੁਖਿ ਨਿਵਾਸੁ; ਫਿਰਿ ਫਿਰਿ ਆਈਐ ॥
Without serving the True Guru, there is no abiding in peace; one comes again and again.
The world is counterfeit capital; it earns only falsehood.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਸਚੁ ਖਰਾ ਸਾਲਾਹਿ; ਪਤਿ ਸਿਉ ਜਾਈਐ ॥੧੪॥
O Nanak, praising the purely True One, one departs with honour. ॥14॥
ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੈ. ਤਾ ਵਾਵਹਿ ਗਾਵਹਿ; ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੈ. ਜਲਿ ਨਾਵਹਿ ॥
When it pleases You, they play music and sing; when it pleases You, they bathe in the water (of pilgrimage).
145: ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵਹਿ. ਤਾ ਕਰਹਿ ਬਿਭੂਤਾ; ਸਿੰਙੀ ਨਾਦੁ ਵਜਾਵਹਿ ॥
When it pleases You, they smear ashes on their bodies and blow the horn and conch.
ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੈ. ਤਾ ਪੜਹਿ ਕਤੇਬਾ; ਮੁਲਾ ਸੇਖ ਕਹਾਵਹਿ ॥
When it pleases You, they read the Islamic scriptures and are called mullahs and shaikhs.
ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੈ. ਤਾ ਹੋਵਹਿ ਰਾਜੇ; ਰਸ ਕਸ ਬਹੁਤੁ ਕਮਾਵਹਿ ॥
When it pleases You, they become kings and enjoy all kinds of tastes.
ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੈ. ਤੇਗ ਵਗਾਵਹਿ; ਸਿਰ ਮੁੰਡੀ ਕਟਿ ਜਾਵਹਿ ॥
When it pleases You, they wield the sword and heads are cut from necks.
ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੈ. ਜਾਹਿ ਦਿਸੰਤਰਿ; ਸੁਣਿ ਗਲਾ ਘਰਿ ਆਵਹਿ ॥
When it pleases You, they go to foreign lands, and hearing the news there, come back home.
ਜਾ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਵੈ. ਨਾਇ ਰਚਾਵਹਿ; ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਣੇ ਤੂੰ ਭਾਵਹਿ ॥
When it pleases You, they are absorbed in the Name; those who walk in Your will are pleasing to You.
ਨਾਨਕੁ ਏਕ ਕਹੈ ਬੇਨੰਤੀ; ਹੋਰਿ ਸਗਲੇ ਕੂੜੁ ਕਮਾਵਹਿ ॥੧॥
Nanak makes one prayer: all others are practising falsehood. ॥1॥
ਜਾ ਤੂੰ ਵਡਾ. ਸਭਿ ਵਡਿਆਂਈਆ; ਚੰਗੈ ਚੰਗਾ ਹੋਈ ॥
Since You are great, all greatness is Yours; from the good, only good comes.
ਜਾ ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਤਾ ਸਭੁ ਕੋ ਸਚਾ; ਕੂੜਾ ਕੋਇ ਨ ਕੋਈ ॥
Since You are true, everyone is true; no one is false.
ਆਖਣੁ ਵੇਖਣੁ ਬੋਲਣੁ ਚਲਣੁ; ਜੀਵਣੁ ਮਰਣਾ ਧਾਤੁ ॥
Speaking and seeing, talking and walking, living and dying — all this is Maya.
ਹੁਕਮੁ ਸਾਜਿ. ਹੁਕਮੈ ਵਿਚਿ ਰਖੈ; ਨਾਨਕ ਸਚਾ ਆਪਿ ॥੨॥
Creating His command, He keeps all within His command; O Nanak, He Himself is the True One. ॥2॥
Serve the True Guru wholeheartedly, and doubt is dispelled.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਆਖੈ ਕਾਰ; ਸੁ ਕਾਰ ਕਮਾਈਐ ॥
Do the work that the True Guru tells you to do.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ; ਤ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ॥
When the True Guru is merciful, one meditates on the Name.
ਲਾਹਾ ਭਗਤਿ ਸੁ ਸਾਰੁ; ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਪਾਈਐ ॥
The excellent profit of devotion is obtained by facing the Guru.
The self-willed earn only falsehood and darkness; they practise falsehood.
ਸਚੇ ਦੈ ਦਰਿ ਜਾਇ; ਸਚੁ ਚਵਾਂਈਐ ॥
Go to the door of the True One and speak the Truth (chant His Name),
and through the True Name you are called into the mansion of the True One.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਸਚੁ ਸਦਾ ਸਚਿਆਰੁ; ਸਚਿ ਸਮਾਈਐ ॥੧੫॥
O Nanak, one who always has Truth is a true trader; he merges in the True One. ॥15॥
ਕਲਿ ਕਾਤੀ. ਰਾਜੇ ਕਾਸਾਈ; ਧਰਮੁ. ਪੰਖ ਕਰਿ ਉਡਰਿਆ ॥
This dark age is a knife, the kings are butchers; righteousness has sprouted wings and flown away.
ਕੂੜੁ ਅਮਾਵਸ. ਸਚੁ ਚੰਦ੍ਰਮਾ; ਦੀਸੈ ਨਾਹੀ. ਕਹ ਚੜਿਆ ॥
Falsehood is the dark night of the new moon; the moon of Truth is nowhere seen to rise.
I have searched until I am distraught;
in the darkness no path is seen.
In ego the world cries out in pain.
ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ; ਕਿਨਿ ਬਿਧਿ ਗਤਿ ਹੋਈ ॥੧॥
Says Nanak, how can there be release? ॥1॥
In this dark age, the Lord's praise is the light made manifest in the world.
Some rare one who faces the Guru crosses over.
ਜਿਸ ਨੋ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇ; ਤਿਸੁ ਦੇਵੈ ॥
The one on whom He casts His glance of grace, He blesses with it.
O Nanak, facing the Guru, that one obtains the jewel (of the Name). ॥2॥
ਭਗਤਾ ਤੈ ਸੈਸਾਰੀਆ; ਜੋੜੁ. ਕਦੇ ਨ ਆਇਆ ॥
Between the devotees and the worldly there has never been any match.
ਕਰਤਾ ਆਪਿ ਅਭੁਲੁ ਹੈ; ਨ ਭੁਲੈ. ਕਿਸੈ ਦਾ ਭੁਲਾਇਆ ॥
The Creator Himself does not err; nor can anyone cause Him to err.
ਭਗਤ ਆਪੇ ਮੇਲਿਅਨੁ; ਜਿਨੀ ਸਚੋ ਸਚੁ ਕਮਾਇਆ ॥
He Himself has united the devotees with Himself; they practise Truth and only Truth.
ਸੈਸਾਰੀ ਆਪਿ ਖੁਆਇਅਨੁ; ਜਿਨੀ ਕੂੜੁ ਬੋਲਿ ਬੋਲਿ ਬਿਖੁ ਖਾਇਆ ॥
He Himself has led the worldly astray; speaking lie after lie, they eat poison.
ਚਲਣ. ਸਾਰ ਨ ਜਾਣਨੀ; ਕਾਮੁ ਕਰੋਧੁ. ਵਿਸੁ ਵਧਾਇਆ ॥
They do not realise that they must depart; they keep increasing the poison of lust and anger.
ਭਗਤ ਕਰਨਿ ਹਰਿ ਚਾਕਰੀ; ਜਿਨੀ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ ॥
The devotees serve the Lord; night and day they meditate on the Name.
ਦਾਸਨਿ ਦਾਸ ਹੋਇ ਕੈ; ਜਿਨੀ. ਵਿਚਹੁ ਆਪੁ ਗਵਾਇਆ ॥
Becoming the slaves of His slaves, they have removed self-conceit from within.
ਓਨਾ ਖਸਮੈ ਕੈ ਦਰਿ ਮੁਖ ਉਜਲੇ; ਸਚੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਸੁਹਾਇਆ ॥੧੬॥
At the Master's door their faces are radiant; they are adorned by the True Word. ॥16॥
ਸਬਾਹੀ ਸਾਲਾਹ; ਜਿਨੀ ਧਿਆਇਆ ਇਕ ਮਨਿ ॥
Those who praise the Lord in the early morning and meditate on Him single-mindedly,
ਸੇਈ ਪੂਰੇ ਸਾਹ; ਵਖਤੈ ਉਪਰਿ ਲੜਿ ਮੁਏ ॥
who battle with their mind at the right time (the ambrosial hour) — they are the perfect kings.
ਦੂਜੈ ਬਹੁਤੇ ਰਾਹ; ਮਨ ਕੀਆ ਮਤੀ ਖਿੰਡੀਆ ॥
In the second watch, the mind's thoughts scatter and run along many paths.
ਬਹੁਤੁ ਪਏ ਅਸਗਾਹ; ਗੋਤੇ ਖਾਹਿ. ਨ ਨਿਕਲਹਿ ॥
Many fall into the bottomless ocean of worldly affairs; they sink and cannot get out.
146: ਤੀਜੈ. ਮੁਹੀ ਗਿਰਾਹ; ਭੁਖ ਤਿਖਾ ਦੁਇ. ਭਉਕੀਆ ॥
In the third watch, hunger and thirst both bark, and they put food in their mouths.
ਖਾਧਾ ਹੋਇ ਸੁਆਹ; ਭੀ ਖਾਣੇ ਸਿਉ ਦੋਸਤੀ ॥
What is eaten turns to ashes, yet the craving for more food remains.
ਚਉਥੈ ਆਈ ਊਂਘ; ਅਖੀ ਮੀਟਿ. ਪਵਾਰਿ ਗਇਆ ॥
In the fourth watch drowsiness comes; they close their eyes and fall fast asleep.
ਭੀ. ਉਠਿ ਰਚਿਓਨੁ ਵਾਦੁ; ਸੈ ਵਰੑਿਆ ਕੀ ਪਿੜ ਬਧੀ ॥
Then rising again, they start the same strife, as if they had set the stage to live a hundred years.
ਸਭੇ ਵੇਲਾ ਵਖਤ ਸਭਿ; ਜੇ ਅਠੀ ਭਉ ਹੋਇ ॥
All times and moments are good, if the fear of God is present through all eight watches.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਸਾਹਿਬੁ ਮਨਿ ਵਸੈ; ਸਚਾ ਨਾਵਣੁ ਹੋਇ ॥੧॥
O Nanak, when the Master dwells in the mind, the true cleansing bath is obtained. ॥1॥
ਸੇਈ ਪੂਰੇ ਸਾਹ; ਜਿਨੀ ਪੂਰਾ ਪਾਇਆ ॥
They alone are perfect kings who have found the Perfect Lord.
Through all eight watches they remain carefree, dyed in the love of the One.
Rare are those found absorbed in the sight and form of the unfathomable Lord.
ਕਰਮਿ ਪੂਰੈ. ਪੂਰਾ ਗੁਰੂ; ਪੂਰਾ ਜਾ ਕਾ ਬੋਲੁ ॥
By perfect destiny one meets the Perfect Guru, whose word is perfect.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਪੂਰਾ ਜੇ ਕਰੇ; ਘਟੈ ਨਾਹੀ. ਤੋਲੁ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, whomever He makes perfect does not fall short in weight. ॥2॥
ਜਾ ਤੂੰ ਤਾ ਕਿਆ ਹੋਰਿ; ਮੈ ਸਚੁ ਸੁਣਾਈਐ ॥
When You are with me, what need have I of anyone else? I speak the truth.
ਮੁਠੀ ਧੰਧੈ ਚੋਰਿ; ਮਹਲੁ ਨ ਪਾਈਐ ॥
The soul-bride robbed by the thief of worldly affairs does not find the mansion of Your presence.
Through her hard heart she has wasted all her service.
ਜਿਤੁ ਘਟਿ. ਸਚੁ ਨ ਪਾਇ; ਸੁ ਭੰਨਿ ਘੜਾਈਐ ॥
The heart in which Truth is not found is broken and refashioned again and again.
ਕਿਉ ਕਰਿ ਪੂਰੈ ਵਟਿ; ਤੋਲਿ ਤੁਲਾਈਐ ॥
How can it be weighed and found full weight against the perfect weight?
ਕੋਇ. ਨ ਆਖੈ ਘਟਿ; ਹਉਮੈ ਜਾਈਐ ॥
No one calls it short-weight when ego departs.
The genuine are assayed and accepted at the door of the all-seeing Lord.
ਸਉਦਾ ਇਕਤੁ ਹਟਿ; ਪੂਰੈ ਗੁਰਿ ਪਾਈਐ ॥੧੭॥
This merchandise is obtained only from one shop, the Perfect Guru. ॥17॥
ਅਠੀ ਪਹਰੀ. ਅਠ ਖੰਡ; ਨਾਵਾ ਖੰਡੁ ਸਰੀਰੁ ॥
Through the eight watches the mind runs after the eight continents; the ninth continent is the body.
ਤਿਸੁ ਵਿਚਿ ਨਉ ਨਿਧਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਏਕੁ; ਭਾਲਹਿ ਗੁਣੀ ਗਹੀਰੁ ॥
Within it are the nine treasures of the One Name; seek out the deep Lord of virtues.
ਕਰਮਵੰਤੀ ਸਾਲਾਹਿਆ; ਨਾਨਕ. ਕਰਿ ਗੁਰੁ ਪੀਰੁ ॥
O Nanak, the fortunate praise the Lord, taking the Guru as their spiritual guide.
ਚਉਥੈ ਪਹਰਿ ਸਬਾਹ ਕੈ; ਸੁਰਤਿਆ ਉਪਜੈ ਚਾਉ ॥
In the fourth watch of the early morning, longing wells up in those of higher awareness.
ਤਿਨਾ ਦਰੀਆਵਾ ਸਿਉ ਦੋਸਤੀ; ਮਨਿ ਮੁਖਿ. ਸਚਾ ਨਾਉ ॥
They befriend those who are rivers (of the Name); the True Name is in their minds and on their lips.
ਓਥੈ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤੁ ਵੰਡੀਐ; ਕਰਮੀ ਹੋਇ ਪਸਾਉ ॥
There the Ambrosial Nectar is distributed, and by His grace they receive the gift.
ਕੰਚਨ ਕਾਇਆ ਕਸੀਐ; ਵੰਨੀ ਚੜੈ ਚੜਾਉ ॥
Like gold, the body is tested on the touchstone, and takes on the beautiful colour (of devotion).
ਜੇ ਹੋਵੈ ਨਦਰਿ ਸਰਾਫ ਕੀ; ਬਹੁੜਿ. ਨ ਪਾਈ ਤਾਉ ॥
When the Assayer casts His glance of grace, it need not be heated in the fire again.
ਸਤੀ ਪਹਰੀ. ਸਤੁ ਭਲਾ; ਬਹੀਐ ਪੜਿਆ ਪਾਸਿ ॥
In the other seven watches, good conduct is needed; sit with the spiritually wise.
ਓਥੈ. ਪਾਪੁ ਪੁੰਨੁ ਬੀਚਾਰੀਐ; ਕੂੜੈ ਘਟੈ ਰਾਸਿ ॥
There good and bad deeds are reflected upon, and the capital of falsehood is reduced.
ਓਥੈ ਖੋਟੇ ਸਟੀਅਹਿ; ਖਰੇ ਕੀਚਹਿ ਸਾਬਾਸਿ ॥
There the counterfeit is cast aside, and the genuine is applauded.
ਬੋਲਣੁ ਫਾਦਲੁ ਨਾਨਕਾ; ਦੁਖੁ ਸੁਖੁ ਖਸਮੈ ਪਾਸਿ ॥੧॥
Complaining is useless, O Nanak; pain and pleasure are in the Master's hands. ॥1॥
ਪਉਣੁ ਗੁਰੂ ਪਾਣੀ ਪਿਤਾ; ਮਾਤਾ ਧਰਤਿ ਮਹਤੁ ॥
Air is the Guru, water the father, and the great earth the mother.
ਦਿਨਸੁ ਰਾਤਿ ਦੁਇ. ਦਾਈ ਦਾਇਆ; ਖੇਲੈ ਸਗਲ ਜਗਤੁ ॥
Day and night are the two nurses, male and female, in whose lap the whole world plays.
Good deeds and bad deeds are read out in the presence of the Lord of righteousness.
ਕਰਮੀ ਆਪੋ ਆਪਣੀ; ਕੇ ਨੇੜੈ ਕੇ ਦੂਰਿ ॥
According to their own actions, some are drawn close and some are driven far away.
ਜਿਨੀ ਨਾਮੁ ਧਿਆਇਆ; ਗਏ ਮਸਕਤਿ ਘਾਲਿ ॥
Those who have meditated on the Name have departed having made their labour fruitful.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਤੇ ਮੁਖ ਉਜਲੇ; ਹੋਰ ਕੇਤੀ ਛੁਟੀ ਨਾਲਿ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, their faces are radiant, and many others are saved along with them. ॥2॥
The one to whom the True Guru has revealed love for the Lord as the true food
is satisfied with the True One alone, and blossoms in the True One.
ਸਚੈ ਕੋਟਿ ਗਿਰਾਂਇ; ਨਿਜ ਘਰਿ ਵਸਿਆ ॥
He dwells in his own true home, as in the fortress and village of the True One.
When the True Guru is pleased, the Name is obtained, and one delights in His love.
ਸਚੈ ਦੈ ਦੀਬਾਣਿ; ਕੂੜਿ. ਨ ਜਾਈਐ ॥
No one reaches the court of the True One through falsehood.
ਝੂਠੋ ਝੂਠੁ ਵਖਾਣਿ; ਸੁ ਮਹਲੁ ਖੁਆਈਐ ॥
Speaking lie after lie, one loses the mansion of His presence.
147: ਸਚੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਨੀਸਾਣਿ; ਠਾਕ. ਨ ਪਾਈਐ ॥
With the True Word as the pass, no one is stopped on the way.
ਸਚੁ ਸੁਣਿ ਬੁਝਿ ਵਖਾਣਿ; ਮਹਲਿ ਬੁਲਾਈਐ ॥੧੮॥
Hearing, understanding and chanting the True Name, one is called into His mansion. ॥18॥
ਪਹਿਰਾ ਅਗਨਿ. ਹਿਵੈ ਘਰੁ ਬਾਧਾ; ਭੋਜਨੁ ਸਾਰੁ ਕਰਾਈ ॥
If I were to wear fire, build my house in snow, and make iron my food;
ਸਗਲੇ ਦੂਖ ਪਾਣੀ ਕਰਿ ਪੀਵਾ; ਧਰਤੀ ਹਾਕ ਚਲਾਈ ॥
if I were to drink all pain like water, and drive the whole earth before me;
ਧਰਿ ਤਾਰਾਜੀ ਅੰਬਰੁ ਤੋਲੀ; ਪਿਛੈ ਟੰਕੁ ਚੜਾਈ ॥
if I could weigh the sky on a scale, balancing it with a small weight;
ਏਵਡੁ ਵਧਾ. ਮਾਵਾ ਨਾਹੀ; ਸਭਸੈ ਨਥਿ ਚਲਾਈ ॥
if I could grow so great that I could be contained nowhere, and lead everyone by the nose;
ਏਤਾ ਤਾਣੁ ਹੋਵੈ ਮਨ ਅੰਦਰਿ; ਕਰੀ ਭਿ ਆਖਿ ਕਰਾਈ ॥
if I had such power in my mind that I could do anything, and have others do it at my word —
ਜੇਵਡੁ ਸਾਹਿਬੁ. ਤੇਵਡ ਦਾਤੀ; ਦੇ ਦੇ ਕਰੇ ਰਜਾਈ ॥
as great as the Master is, so great are His gifts; He gives them as He wills.
ਨਾਨਕ ਨਦਰਿ. ਕਰੇ ਜਿਸੁ ਉਪਰਿ; ਸਚਿ; ਨਾਮਿ ਵਡਿਆਈ ॥੧॥
O Nanak, the one on whom He casts His glance of grace is given glory through the True Name. ॥1॥
ਆਖਣੁ. ਆਖਿ ਨ ਰਜਿਆ; ਸੁਨਣਿ. ਨ ਰਜੇ ਕੰਨ ॥
The mouth is not satisfied with speaking, nor are the ears satisfied with hearing.
ਅਖੀ. ਦੇਖਿ ਨ ਰਜੀਆ; ਗੁਣ ਗਾਹਕ ਇਕ ਵੰਨ ॥
The eyes are not satisfied with seeing; each sense is a customer for its own kind of taste.
ਭੁਖਿਆ. ਭੁਖ ਨ ਉਤਰੈ; ਗਲੀ ਭੁਖ. ਨ ਜਾਇ ॥
The hunger of the hungry is not relieved; mere words do not take hunger away.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਭੁਖਾ ਤਾ ਰਜੈ; ਜਾ ਗੁਣ ਕਹਿ. ਗੁਣੀ ਸਮਾਇ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, the hungry is satisfied only when, chanting the praises of the Lord of virtues, he merges in Him. ॥2॥
ਵਿਣੁ ਸਚੇ ਸਭੁ ਕੂੜੁ; ਕੂੜੁ ਕਮਾਈਐ ॥
Without the True One, all is false; one earns only falsehood.
Without the True One, the false are bound and driven along.
ਵਿਣੁ ਸਚੇ. ਤਨੁ ਛਾਰੁ; ਛਾਰੁ ਰਲਾਈਐ ॥
Without the True One, the body is dust, and it mingles with dust.
ਵਿਣੁ ਸਚੇ. ਸਭ ਭੁਖ; ਜਿ ਪੈਝੈ ਖਾਈਐ ॥
Without the True One, all that one wears and eats only increases hunger.
ਵਿਣੁ ਸਚੇ ਦਰਬਾਰੁ; ਕੂੜਿ ਨ ਪਾਈਐ ॥
Without the True One, the Court is not reached through falsehood.
Attached to false greed, one loses the mansion of His presence.
ਸਭੁ ਜਗੁ ਠਗਿਓ ਠਗਿ; ਆਈਐ ਜਾਈਐ ॥
The whole world is cheated by the cheat (of falsehood), and comes and goes.
ਤਨ ਮਹਿ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਨਾ ਅਗਿ; ਸਬਦਿ ਬੁਝਾਈਐ ॥੧੯॥
The fire of craving within the body is quenched through the Word. ॥19॥
ਨਾਨਕ. ਗੁਰੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੁ ਰੁਖੁ; ਧਰਮੁ ਫੁਲੁ. ਫਲ ਗਿਆਨੁ ॥
O Nanak, the Guru is the tree of contentment, with righteousness as its flower and spiritual wisdom its fruit.
ਰਸਿ ਰਸਿਆ. ਹਰਿਆ ਸਦਾ; ਪਕੈ. ਕਰਮਿ ਧਿਆਨਿ ॥
Watered with love, it stays forever green; through His grace and meditation it ripens.
ਪਤਿ ਕੇ ਸਾਦ ਖਾਦਾ ਲਹੈ; ਦਾਨਾ ਕੈ ਸਿਰਿ ਦਾਨੁ ॥੧॥
One who eats it enjoys the delight of union with the Lord; of all gifts, this is the greatest gift. ॥1॥
ਸੁਇਨੇ ਕਾ ਬਿਰਖੁ. ਪਤ ਪਰਵਾਲਾ; ਫੁਲ ਜਵੇਹਰ ਲਾਲ ॥
The Guru is a tree of gold, its leaves coral, its flowers jewels and rubies.
ਤਿਤੁ. ਫਲ ਰਤਨ ਲਗਹਿ. ਮੁਖਿ ਭਾਖਿਤ; ਹਿਰਦੈ ਰਿਦੈ ਨਿਹਾਲੁ ॥
It bears the fruit of jewels — the words spoken from his mouth; within his heart he is ever in bliss.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਕਰਮੁ ਹੋਵੈ ਮੁਖਿ ਮਸਤਕਿ; ਲਿਖਿਆ ਹੋਵੈ ਲੇਖੁ ॥
O Nanak, one who receives His grace, with destiny written on his forehead,
ਅਠਿਸਠਿ ਤੀਰਥ ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਚਰਣੀ; ਪੂਜੈ ਸਦਾ ਵਿਸੇਖੁ ॥
worships the Guru's feet, knowing them as more sacred than the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage.
ਹੰਸੁ ਹੇਤੁ ਲੋਭੁ ਕੋਪੁ; ਚਾਰੇ ਨਦੀਆ ਅਗਿ ॥
Cruelty, attachment, greed and anger are the four rivers of fire.
ਪਵਹਿ ਦਝਹਿ ਨਾਨਕਾ; ਤਰੀਐ ਕਰਮੀ ਲਗਿ ॥੨॥
Those who fall into them are burnt, O Nanak; one crosses over only by His grace, clinging to the Guru. ॥2॥
Conquer (craving) and die while yet alive, so that you do not regret it in the end.
Rare is the one who has understood that this world is false.
ਸਚਿ. ਨ ਧਰੇ ਪਿਆਰੁ; ਧੰਧੈ ਧਾਈਐ ॥
One does not love the Truth, but runs about after worldly affairs.
ਕਾਲੁ ਬੁਰਾ. ਖੈ ਕਾਲੁ; ਸਿਰਿ ਦੁਨੀਆਈਐ ॥
Terrible death, the destroyer, hovers over the head of the world.
By His command, the Messenger of Death stands over every head and strikes when he gets his chance.
The Lord Himself gives His love and makes Himself dwell in the mind.
ਮੁਹਤੁ ਨ ਚਸਾ ਵਿਲੰਮੁ; ਭਰੀਐ ਪਾਈਐ ॥
When the measure of life is full, not a moment's delay is allowed.
By the Guru's grace, one understands this and merges in the True One. ॥20॥
ਤੁਮੀ ਤੁਮਾ ਵਿਸੁ; ਅਕੁ ਧਤੂਰਾ ਨਿਮੁ ਫਲੁ ॥
Bitter melon, poison, swallow-wort, thorn-apple and the neem fruit
ਮਨਿ ਮੁਖਿ ਵਸਹਿ ਤਿਸੁ; ਜਿਸੁ ਤੂੰ. ਚਿਤਿ ਨ ਆਵਹੀ ॥
dwell in the mind and mouth of the one who does not keep You in mind.
ਨਾਨਕ ਕਹੀਐ ਕਿਸੁ; ਹੰਢਨਿ ਕਰਮਾ ਬਾਹਰੇ ॥੧॥
O Nanak, to whom can this be told? Such unfortunate ones wander about. ॥1॥
ਮਤਿ ਪੰਖੇਰੂ. ਕਿਰਤੁ ਸਾਥਿ; ਕਬ ਉਤਮ ਕਬ ਨੀਚ ॥
The intellect is a bird, with its past deeds as its companion; sometimes it is high, sometimes low.
148: ਕਬ ਚੰਦਨਿ. ਕਬ ਅਕਿ ਡਾਲਿ; ਕਬ ਉਚੀ ਪਰੀਤਿ ॥
Sometimes it sits on the sandalwood tree, sometimes on the branch of swallow-wort; sometimes it soars in lofty love.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਹੁਕਮਿ ਚਲਾਈਐ; ਸਾਹਿਬ ਲਗੀ ਰੀਤਿ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, all are driven by His command; this is the way of the Master. ॥2॥
ਕੇਤੇ ਕਹਹਿ ਵਖਾਣ; ਕਹਿ ਕਹਿ ਜਾਵਣਾ ॥
Countless have described Him, and having described Him, have departed.
ਵੇਦ ਕਹਹਿ ਵਖਿਆਣ; ਅੰਤੁ ਨ ਪਾਵਣਾ ॥
The Vedas give their explanations, but no one has found His limit.
His mystery is not found by reading; it is grasped through understanding.
ਖਟੁ ਦਰਸਨ ਕੈ ਭੇਖਿ; ਕਿਸੈ ਸਚਿ ਸਮਾਵਣਾ ॥
Through the garbs of the six schools, has anyone merged in the True One?
The True Lord is unseen; He appears beautiful through the Word.
One who believes in the Name of the countless Lord reaches His court.
He bows to the Creator, and sings His praises as His minstrel.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਜੁਗੁ ਜੁਗੁ ਏਕੁ; ਮੰਨਿ ਵਸਾਵਣਾ ॥੨੧॥
O Nanak, he enshrines in his mind the One who exists in every age. ॥21॥
ਮੰਤ੍ਰੀ ਹੋਇ ਅਠੂਹਿਆ; ਨਾਗੀ ਲਗੈ ਜਾਇ ॥
One who is a charmer only of scorpions and goes to grab hold of snakes
ਆਪਣ ਹਥੀ ਆਪਣੈ; ਦੇ ਕੂਚਾ ਆਪੇ ਲਾਇ ॥
sets himself on fire with his own hands.
ਹੁਕਮੁ ਪਇਆ. ਧੁਰਿ ਖਸਮ ਕਾ; ਅਤੀ ਹੂ ਧਕਾ ਖਾਇ ॥
By the Master's primal command, he suffers a blow for his excess.
ਗੁਰਮੁਖ ਸਿਉ. ਮਨਮੁਖੁ ਅੜੈ; ਡੁਬੈ. ਹਕਿ ਨਿਆਇ ॥
When the self-willed clashes with the Guru-facing, he drowns, by true justice.
ਦੁਹਾ ਸਿਰਿਆ. ਆਪੇ ਖਸਮੁ; ਵੇਖੈ. ਕਰਿ ਵਿਉਪਾਇ ॥
The Master Himself is over both sides; He watches and judges.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਏਵੈ ਜਾਣੀਐ; ਸਭ ਕਿਛੁ ਤਿਸਹਿ ਰਜਾਇ ॥੧॥
O Nanak, know it thus: all is in His will. ॥1॥
ਨਾਨਕ. ਪਰਖੇ ਆਪ ਕਉ; ਤਾ ਪਾਰਖੁ ਜਾਣੁ ॥
O Nanak, if one assays oneself, then know him to be a true assayer.
ਰੋਗੁ ਦਾਰੂ ਦੋਵੈ ਬੁਝੈ; ਤਾ ਵੈਦੁ ਸੁਜਾਣੁ ॥
If one understands both the disease and the cure, then he is a wise physician.
ਵਾਟ. ਨ ਕਰਈ ਮਾਮਲਾ; ਜਾਣੈ ਮਿਹਮਾਣੁ ॥
He does not get into quarrels on the way; he knows himself to be a guest.
ਮੂਲੁ ਜਾਣਿ ਗਲਾ ਕਰੇ; ਹਾਣਿ ਲਾਏ ਹਾਣੁ ॥
Knowing his origin, he speaks; he spends his time with his own kind.
ਲਬਿ. ਨ ਚਲਈ. ਸਚਿ ਰਹੈ; ਸੋ ਵਿਸਟੁ ਪਰਵਾਣੁ ॥
One who does not act out of greed and abides in the Truth is an approved guide.
ਸਰੁ ਸੰਧੇ ਆਗਾਸ ਕਉ; ਕਿਉ ਪਹੁਚੈ ਬਾਣੁ ॥
If one shoots an arrow at the sky, how can the arrow reach it?
ਅਗੈ. ਓਹੁ ਅਗੰਮੁ ਹੈ; ਵਾਹੇਦੜੁ ਜਾਣੁ ॥੨॥
The sky beyond is unreachable; know that the arrow falls back on the archer. ॥2॥
The soul-brides who love their Husband are adorned with His love.
ਕਰਨਿ ਭਗਤਿ. ਦਿਨੁ ਰਾਤਿ; ਨ ਰਹਨੀ. ਵਾਰੀਆ ॥
They worship Him day and night, and do not stop even when forbidden.
Reformed by the Word, they dwell within His mansion.
Being wise, they make the true prayer.
Having reached Him by His command, they look beautiful at their Master's side.
Loving Him with all their heart, they pray to Him as His companions.
ਬਿਨੁ ਨਾਵੈ. ਧ੍ਰਿਗੁ ਵਾਸੁ; ਫਿਟੁ ਸੁ ਜੀਵਿਆ ॥
Cursed is the dwelling, and cursed the life, without the Name.
The one whom He has reformed through the Word has drunk the Ambrosial Nectar. ॥22॥
ਮਾਰੂ. ਮੀਹਿ ਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਪਤਿਆ; ਅਗੀ. ਲਹੈ ਨ ਭੁਖ ॥
The desert is not satisfied by rain, and the hunger of fire is not satisfied.
ਰਾਜਾ. ਰਾਜਿ ਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਪਤਿਆ; ਸਾਇਰ ਭਰੇ. ਕਿਸੁਕ ॥
The king is not satisfied by his kingdom; what can drought do to the full ocean?
ਨਾਨਕ ਸਚੇ ਨਾਮ ਕੀ; ਕੇਤੀ ਪੁਛਾ ਪੁਛ ॥੧॥
O Nanak, how great is the longing for the True Name? It cannot be told. ॥1॥
ਨਿਹਫਲੰ. ਤਸਿ ਜਨਮਸਿ; ਜਾਵਤੁ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ. ਨ ਬਿੰਦਤੇ ॥
Fruitless is one's life as long as one does not know God.
ਸਾਗਰੰ ਸੰਸਾਰਸਿ; ਗੁਰ ਪਰਸਾਦੀ ਤਰਹਿ ਕੇ ॥
By the Guru's grace, some cross over the world-ocean.
ਕਰਣ ਕਾਰਣ ਸਮਰਥੁ ਹੈ; ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਬੀਚਾਰਿ ॥
The Lord, the Cause of causes, is all-powerful; says Nanak, reflect on Him.
ਕਾਰਣੁ ਕਰਤੇ ਵਸਿ ਹੈ; ਜਿਨਿ ਕਲ ਰਖੀ ਧਾਰਿ ॥੨॥
The creation is under the control of the Creator, who has upheld it by His power. ॥2॥
The minstrel (who sings His praises) dwells in the Master's court.
Praising the True Master, the lotus of his heart blossoms.
Obtaining the perfect state from the Master, his mind is delighted.
He drives out and destroys his enemies (the vices), and his friends (the senses) rejoice.
ਸਚਾ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਸੇਵਨਿ; ਸਚਾ ਮਾਰਗੁ ਦਸਿਆ ॥
Those who serve the True Guru are shown the true path.
149: Reflecting on the True Word, he destroys (the fear of) death.
Reformed by the Word, the minstrel speaks of the indescribable Lord.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਗੁਣ ਗਹਿ ਰਾਸਿ; ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ ਮਿਲੇ ਪਿਆਰਿਆ ॥੨੩॥
O Nanak, gathering the wealth of virtues, he meets his Beloved Lord. ॥23॥
ਖਤਿਅਹੁ ਜੰਮੇ. ਖਤੇ ਕਰਨਿ; ਤ ਖਤਿਆ ਵਿਚਿ ਪਾਹਿ ॥
Born because of sins, they commit sins, and fall into sins again.
ਧੋਤੇ. ਮੂਲਿ ਨ ਉਤਰਹਿ; ਜੇ ਸਉ ਧੋਵਣ ਪਾਹਿ ॥
These sins are not removed at all by washing, even if washed a hundred times.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਬਖਸੇ ਬਖਸੀਅਹਿ; ਨਾਹਿ ਤ. ਪਾਹੀ ਪਾਹਿ ॥੧॥
O Nanak, if He forgives, they are forgiven; otherwise one is beaten with shoes. ॥1॥
ਨਾਨਕ. ਬੋਲਣੁ ਝਖਣਾ; ਦੁਖ ਛਡਿ ਮੰਗੀਅਹਿ ਸੁਖ ॥
O Nanak, it is mere idle chatter to ask for pleasure while rejecting pain.
ਸੁਖੁ ਦੁਖੁ ਦੁਇ. ਦਰਿ ਕਪੜੇ; ਪਹਿਰਹਿ ਜਾਇ ਮਨੁਖ ॥
Pleasure and pain are the two garments given at His door, which people come into the world to wear.
ਜਿਥੈ ਬੋਲਣਿ ਹਾਰੀਐ; ਤਿਥੈ ਚੰਗੀ ਚੁਪ ॥੨॥
Where speaking only ends in defeat, silence is best. ॥2॥
Having looked in all four directions, one who searches within
sees that the True, unseen Lord has created and is watching over the creation.
To those lost in the wilderness, the Guru has shown the way.
Hail to the True Guru, through whom the True One is remembered.
The jewel is found within one's own home, when the lamp (of wisdom) is lit.
ਸਚੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਸਲਾਹਿ; ਸੁਖੀਏ ਸਚ ਵਾਲਿਆ ॥
Praising Him through the True Word, those who belong to the True One are at peace.
ਨਿਡਰਿਆ ਡਰੁ ਲਗਿ; ਗਰਬਿ ਸਿ ਗਾਲਿਆ ॥
Those who do not fear God are gripped by other fears; they are consumed by their pride.
Forgetting the Name, the world wanders about out of step. ॥24॥
ਭੈ ਵਿਚਿ ਜੰਮੈ. ਭੈ ਮਰੈ; ਭੀ ਭਉ ਮਨ ਮਹਿ ਹੋਇ ॥
In fear one is born, in fear one dies, and fear always remains in the mind.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਭੈ ਵਿਚਿ ਜੇ ਮਰੈ; ਸਹਿਲਾ ਆਇਆ ਸੋਇ ॥੧॥
O Nanak, one who dies (to self) in the fear of God — blessed is his coming into the world. ॥1॥
ਭੈ ਵਿਣੁ ਜੀਵੈ ਬਹੁਤੁ ਬਹੁਤੁ; ਖੁਸੀਆ ਖੁਸੀ ਕਮਾਇ ॥
Without the fear of God, one may live very, very long and enjoy every pleasure;
ਨਾਨਕ. ਭੈ ਵਿਣੁ ਜੇ ਮਰੈ; ਮੁਹਿ ਕਾਲੈ ਉਠਿ ਜਾਇ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, if one dies without the fear of God, he departs with a blackened face. ॥2॥
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ; ਤ ਸਰਧਾ ਪੂਰੀਐ ॥
When the True Guru is merciful, faith is fulfilled.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ; ਨ ਕਬਹੂੰ ਝੂਰੀਐ ॥
When the True Guru is merciful, one never grieves.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ; ਤਾ ਦੁਖੁ. ਨ ਜਾਣੀਐ ॥
When the True Guru is merciful, one does not know pain.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ; ਤਾ ਹਰਿ ਰੰਗੁ ਮਾਣੀਐ ॥
When the True Guru is merciful, one enjoys the Lord's love.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ; ਤਾ ਜਮ ਕਾ ਡਰੁ ਕੇਹਾ ॥
When the True Guru is merciful, why fear death?
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ; ਤਾ ਸਦ ਹੀ ਸੁਖੁ ਦੇਹਾ ॥
When the True Guru is merciful, the body is ever at peace.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ; ਤਾ ਨਵ ਨਿਧਿ ਪਾਈਐ ॥
When the True Guru is merciful, the nine treasures are obtained.
ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇ ਦਇਆਲੁ; ਤ ਸਚਿ ਸਮਾਈਐ ॥੨੫॥
When the True Guru is merciful, one merges in the True One. ॥25॥
ਸਿਰੁ ਖੋਹਾਇ. ਪੀਅਹਿ ਮਲਵਾਣੀ; ਜੂਠਾ ਮੰਗਿ ਮੰਗਿ ਖਾਹੀ ॥
They pluck out the hair of their heads, drink filthy water, and beg for and eat others' leftovers.
ਫੋਲਿ ਫਦੀਹਤਿ. ਮੁਹਿ ਲੈਨਿ ਭੜਾਸਾ; ਪਾਣੀ ਦੇਖਿ ਸਗਾਹੀ ॥
They spread out their own excrement, inhale its stench, and shrink from water.
ਭੇਡਾ ਵਾਗੀ. ਸਿਰੁ ਖੋਹਾਇਨਿ; ਭਰੀਅਨਿ ਹਥ ਸੁਆਹੀ ॥
Like sheep, they have their heads plucked, and the pluckers' hands are filled with ashes.
ਮਾਊ ਪੀਊ ਕਿਰਤੁ ਗਵਾਇਨਿ; ਟਬਰ ਰੋਵਨਿ ਧਾਹੀ ॥
They abandon the work of their mothers and fathers, and their families cry and wail.
ਓਨਾ. ਪਿੰਡੁ ਨ ਪਤਲਿ. ਕਿਰਿਆ ਨ ਦੀਵਾ; ਮੁਏ. ਕਿਥਾਊ ਪਾਹੀ ॥
No rice-ball offering, no leaf-plate, no last rites, no lamp — when they die, who knows where they go?
ਅਠਸਠਿ ਤੀਰਥ. ਦੇਨਿ ਨ ਢੋਈ; ਬ੍ਰਹਮਣ. ਅੰਨੁ ਨ ਖਾਹੀ ॥
The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage give them no shelter, and no Brahmin will eat their food.
ਸਦਾ ਕੁਚੀਲ ਰਹਹਿ. ਦਿਨੁ ਰਾਤੀ; ਮਥੈ ਟਿਕੇ ਨਾਹੀ ॥
They remain filthy day and night, and wear no ceremonial mark on their foreheads.
ਝੁੰਡੀ ਪਾਇ ਬਹਨਿ ਨਿਤਿ. ਮਰਣੈ; ਦੜਿ ਦੀਬਾਣਿ. ਨ ਜਾਹੀ ॥
They always sit with bowed heads as if in mourning, and never go to any holy gathering.
ਲਕੀ ਕਾਸੇ ਹਥੀ ਫੁੰਮਣ; ਅਗੋ ਪਿਛੀ ਜਾਹੀ ॥
With bowls hanging at their waists and dusters in their hands, they walk in single file.
ਨਾ ਓਇ ਜੋਗੀ. ਨਾ ਓਇ ਜੰਗਮ; ਨਾ ਓਇ ਕਾਜੀ ਮੁੰਲਾ ॥
They are neither yogis, nor Jangams, nor Qazis or mullahs.
150: ਦਯਿ ਵਿਗੋਏ. ਫਿਰਹਿ ਵਿਗੁਤੇ; ਫਿਟਾ ਵਤੈ ਗਲਾ ॥
Cast off by God, they wander about disgraced; the whole lot of them is cursed.
ਜੀਆ ਮਾਰਿ ਜੀਵਾਲੇ ਸੋਈ; ਅਵਰੁ. ਨ ਕੋਈ ਰਖੈ ॥
He alone kills and revives all beings; no one else can preserve them.
ਦਾਨਹੁ ਤੈ ਇਸਨਾਨਹੁ ਵੰਜੇ; ਭਸੁ ਪਈ ਸਿਰਿ ਖੁਥੈ ॥
They are deprived of charity and cleansing baths; dust falls on their plucked heads.
ਪਾਣੀ ਵਿਚਹੁ ਰਤਨ ਉਪੰਨੇ; ਮੇਰੁ ਕੀਆ ਮਾਧਾਣੀ ॥
From the water came forth the jewels, when Mount Meru was made the churning stick.
ਅਠਸਠਿ ਤੀਰਥ. ਦੇਵੀ ਥਾਪੇ; ਪੁਰਬੀ ਲਗੈ ਬਾਣੀ ॥
The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage were established for the gods, where festivals are held and sacred discourses recited.
ਨਾਇ ਨਿਵਾਜਾ. ਨਾਤੈ ਪੂਜਾ; ਨਾਵਨਿ ਸਦਾ. ਸੁਜਾਣੀ ॥
After bathing, Muslims say their prayers; after bathing, Hindus worship; the wise always bathe.
ਮੁਇਆ ਜੀਵਦਿਆ ਗਤਿ ਹੋਵੈ; ਜਾਂ ਸਿਰਿ ਪਾਈਐ ਪਾਣੀ ॥
At death and in life, one is purified when water is poured on the head.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਸਿਰਖੁਥੇ ਸੈਤਾਨੀ; ਏਨਾ. ਗਲ ਨ ਭਾਣੀ ॥
O Nanak, these plucked-headed ones are devilish; this teaching does not please them.
ਵੁਠੈ ਹੋਇਐ ਹੋਇ ਬਿਲਾਵਲੁ; ਜੀਆ ਜੁਗਤਿ ਸਮਾਣੀ ॥
When the rain falls there is happiness; the way of life of all beings rests in it.
ਵੁਠੈ. ਅੰਨੁ ਕਮਾਦੁ ਕਪਾਹਾ; ਸਭਸੈ ਪੜਦਾ ਹੋਵੈ ॥
When the rain falls, grain, sugarcane and cotton grow, which provide a covering for all.
ਵੁਠੈ. ਘਾਹੁ ਚਰਹਿ ਨਿਤਿ ਸੁਰਹੀ; ਸਾ ਧਨ ਦਹੀ ਵਿਲੋਵੈ ॥
When the rain falls, the cows graze on grass, and the woman of the house churns the curd into butter.
ਤਿਤੁ ਘਿਇ. ਹੋਮ ਜਗ ਸਦ ਪੂਜਾ; ਪਇਐ ਕਾਰਜੁ ਸੋਹੈ ॥
With that ghee, fire-offerings, sacrifices and worship are performed; with it every rite is graced.
ਗੁਰੂ ਸਮੁੰਦੁ. ਨਦੀ ਸਭਿ ਸਿਖੀ; ਨਾਤੈ ਜਿਤੁ ਵਡਿਆਈ ॥
The Guru is the ocean, and all his teachings are the rivers; bathing in them, glory is obtained.
ਨਾਨਕ. ਜੇ ਸਿਰਖੁਥੇ ਨਾਵਨਿ ਨਾਹੀ; ਤਾ ਸਤ ਚਟੇ ਸਿਰਿ ਛਾਈ ॥੧॥
O Nanak, if these plucked-headed ones do not bathe in it, they earn only ashes on their heads. ॥1॥
ਅਗੀ. ਪਾਲਾ ਕਿ ਕਰੇ; ਸੂਰਜ. ਕੇਹੀ ਰਾਤਿ ॥
What can cold do to fire? What can night do to the sun?
ਚੰਦ. ਅਨੇਰਾ ਕਿ ਕਰੇ; ਪਉਣ ਪਾਣੀ ਕਿਆ ਜਾਤਿ ॥
What can darkness do to the moon? What can caste do to air and water?
ਧਰਤੀ ਚੀਜੀ ਕਿ ਕਰੇ; ਜਿਸੁ ਵਿਚਿ ਸਭੁ ਕਿਛੁ ਹੋਇ ॥
What can things do to the earth, from which everything is produced?
ਨਾਨਕ. ਤਾ ਪਤਿ ਜਾਣੀਐ; ਜਾ ਪਤਿ ਰਖੈ ਸੋਇ ॥੨॥
O Nanak, know that honour to be true which the Lord Himself preserves. ॥2॥
O True Lord, I praise You forever, saying, "Glory to You!"
ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਦੀਬਾਣੁ; ਹੋਰਿ ਆਵਣ ਜਾਣਿਆ ॥
You are the True Ruler; all others come and go.
ਸਚੁ ਜਿ ਮੰਗਹਿ ਦਾਨੁ; ਸਿ ਤੁਧੈ ਜੇਹਿਆ ॥
Those who ask You for the gift of Truth become like You.
True is Your command; through the Word it seems sweet to them.
ਮੰਨਿਐ ਗਿਆਨੁ ਧਿਆਨੁ; ਤੁਧੈ ਤੇ ਪਾਇਆ ॥
Through obeying it, they receive spiritual wisdom and meditation from You.
ਕਰਮਿ ਪਵੈ ਨੀਸਾਨੁ; ਨ ਚਲੈ ਚਲਾਇਆ ॥
By Your grace the insignia is stamped upon them, which no one can erase.
ਤੂੰ ਸਚਾ ਦਾਤਾਰੁ; ਨਿਤ ਦੇਵਹਿ ਚੜਹਿ ਸਵਾਇਆ ॥
You are the True Giver; You give every day, and Your gifts keep increasing.
ਨਾਨਕੁ ਮੰਗੈ ਦਾਨੁ; ਜੋ ਤੁਧੁ ਭਾਇਆ ॥੨੬॥
Nanak begs for the gift that pleases You. ॥26॥
ਦੀਖਿਆ ਆਖਿ ਬੁਝਾਇਆ; ਸਿਫਤੀ ਸਚਿ ਸਮੇਉ ॥
Those whom the Guru has instructed and given understanding, absorbing them in the True One through His praise —
ਤਿਨ ਕਉ ਕਿਆ ਉਪਦੇਸੀਐ; ਜਿਨ ਗੁਰੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਦੇਉ ॥੧॥
what further instruction can they need, who have Guru Nanak as their Guru? ॥1॥
Only the one to whom He gives understanding understands.
ਜਿਸੁ ਆਪਿ ਸੁਝਾਏ; ਤਿਸੁ ਸਭੁ ਕਿਛੁ ਸੂਝੈ ॥
The one whom He Himself enlightens understands everything.
One who merely talks and talks keeps burning in Maya.
By His command He creates all forms.
He Himself knows the thoughts of all.
O Nanak, the Imperishable Lord Himself has spoken the Word;
the one who receives this gift is rid of doubt. ॥2॥
I was a minstrel without work; the Lord put me to His work.
ਰਾਤਿ ਦਿਹੈ ਕੈ ਵਾਰ; ਧੁਰਹੁ ਫੁਰਮਾਇਆ ॥
From the very beginning He commanded me to sing His praises night and day.
The Master has summoned me, His minstrel, to His True Mansion.
He has dressed me in the robe of His true praise and glory.
The True Ambrosial Name has become my food.
ਗੁਰਮਤੀ ਖਾਧਾ ਰਜਿ; ਤਿਨਿ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ ॥
Those who follow the Guru's teaching and eat their fill of it find peace.
His minstrel sings the Word and spreads (and enjoys) His bounty.
ਨਾਨਕ ਸਚੁ ਸਾਲਾਹਿ; ਪੂਰਾ ਪਾਇਆ ॥੨੭॥ ਸੁਧੁ
O Nanak, praising the True One, the Perfect Lord is obtained. ॥27॥ Sudh
